correctness.rationale: The product coordinate v=xy−1 obeys F(v)=(7v−v³)/6, increases to 1, and has summable forward defects since (1−F(v))/(1−v)=(6−v−v²)/6. Thus the coordinate product L converges to a positive finite limit and y converges to 2/(x₀L). At the repeller the analytic Koenigs coordinate has h′(0)=1 and is odd by uniqueness. Pullback by the increasing analytic inverse g gives h′>0 throughout (0,1); forward iterates show its range is (0,∞). Analyticity of the two products follows by pulling into complex neighborhoods of the attracting fixed points for F and g respectively, where the factors approach one geometrically. The one-step identities cancel exactly in A, giving the periodic analytic phase. From gʲ(v)=h⁻¹(λ⁻ʲh(v)) the summable linear terms give B(v)=1−2v+O(v²); the phase change from h(v)/v=1+O(v²) is uniformly O(v²) relatively by positivity and bounded derivative. Independently checked all three tails using q=.9: the forward log tail is at most 5w_N; the backward product tail is at least 1−3z_N by the sum-of-defects bound; summing z_{N+j}²/(7−z_{N+j}²) gives less than z_N² for the Koenigs tail. Independently bracketed both reported amplitudes inside their published decimal intervals and obtained a certified lower difference exceeding 1.2906×10⁻²⁴.
residual_risks: The replay relies on correct rounding of Python decimal ln/exp; it is not formal verification. Only the specified strip and d=1/3 are reviewed. The certificate is of nonconstancy, not a full oscillation range or least period.
